_comment: The naming lines: what Nina says when a prop is TAPPED rather than dragged. Separate from script-keuken.json because it is a whole layer rather than a step in a round — every room after this one will bring its own naming lines for its own props, and VoiceBank loads every bundled script-*.json, so a new room is a new file rather than an edit to a shared one.
_generated: 2026-08-16 — the kitchen's props, then room 6.4's, then room 6.2's

_why._comment: Owner's ask, 2026-08-16: 'make sure we have a small voice over telling what an ingredient / item is when you tap it instead of dragging it. teaches things like this.' It splits the game's two verbs cleanly for the first time — a DRAG is the round, a TAP is the room explaining itself — and it turns the eighteen props that previously answered a tap with a wobble and a sound into eighteen Dutch words.
_why.one_variant_each: Every other line id in the game has two or three variants and never plays the same one twice running, because a character who repeats herself does not sound like a person. These are the exception and it is deliberate: a name is a thing you learn by hearing it the same way twice. Repetition is the feature.
_why.shape: Name first, then one short thing about it. Never longer than two clauses — she is four, and a tap she has to sit through is a tap she stops making. The longest here is 4.9 s and most are near 3.
_why.priority: They are all said at .low priority, which VoiceBank drops outright if anyone is already speaking. A naming line must never talk over the step instruction it would be explaining.
_why.de_tuin_gate_and_bench: Two more when the garden's walls were replaced by a fence — nina.dit.poort for the gate, and nina.dit.werkbank for the potting bench the seed jars moved onto. The garden had been borrowing nina.dit.deur, whose line is 'daarachter is nog een kamer' — true of a door in a kitchen wall, and not of a gate in a garden fence. That id is now the kitchen's alone.
_why.de_tuin: Thirteen more added 2026-08-16 for the garden — zaadje, zaaibak, gat, gieter, plantje, hek, bloemen, molshoop, vlinder, bij, vijver, boom, struik. The eight seed jars are deliberately NOT among them: a jar of aardbei seeds is named through nina.dit.aardbei, the same line the kitchen says when she taps the berry itself, so the word she learns in the garden is the word she hears in the kitchen. nina.dit.mandje and nina.dit.potje are reused unchanged.
_why.no_comment_objects_in_lines: Every element of `lines` must be a real {id, character, variants} object. VoiceBank decodes the array with a non-optional model, so a single `{"_section": "..."}` marker slipped in for readability makes the WHOLE file fail to decode — and it fails silently, into a room where every naming line is mute. Section notes go here in `_why`, never in `lines`.

_rooms.tuin: Fifteen ids added with room 6.2: the seed, the potting bench, the hole, the watering can, the growing plant, the fence, the gate, and the six toys — flowers, molehill, butterfly, bee, pond, tree and bush. nina.dit.plas went out with the garden's two puddles on 2026-08-16: the pond that replaced them is a vijver, and a naming line that says the wrong word is worse than no naming line. One variant each, like the rest of the file.
